svg.aria-label: Roof plan of the Zero Mile Hall and the Mall: a seven-lobed shell with radial skylight ribs around a central oculus, joined to a waisted spine with wave skylights and the piers of concourses A and B.
svg.text: THE ROOF · ZERO MILE HALL AND THE MALL
Seven lobes
Like the segments of a Nagpur orange. Each lobe
is a check-in and security hall; the valleys
between them carry structure and monsoon
rainwater.
The oculus
A glass eye over the Zero Mile marker in the
floor: the one point every departing passenger
crosses.
The Mall
A waisted spine, widest where each concourse
meets it. The automated people mover runs
underneath, one station per concourse.
Piers
Concourses A and B shown. Gates line both
faces; walks from the spine to the farthest
gate stay under 800 m.
Skylights are small and many, not big and few: each lets in a soft patch of light while the shell stays thick and insulated against 47 °C afternoons.
Deep overhangs shade the curtain walls. Light-coloured roof membrane reflects heat. Rainwater from the monsoon is collected in the lobes' valleys.
